https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5yl.text: Image source, Getty Images By James Gregory Published 1 September 2026, 16:43 BST Updated 3 minutes ago Germany has said Russia was responsible for last month's drone attack at Leipzig's airport. A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, close to Ukrainian cargo planes, on 4 August. It failed to explode as the detonator was apparently faulty, and investigators suspect a second drone collided with a cargo aircraft nearby. A third drone was reportedly found near the airport 10 days later. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the Leipzig airport attack followed the "well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe" and the assumption was that Germany would be targeted again. Security experts had speculated that Russia may have been responsible, however Russia has always rejected claims of involvement. Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carries most of the country's aerial cargo. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, who was standing beside Dobrindt at a press conference in Berlin, said he would order the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, and the contract for the Russian House in Berlin will also be terminated - which many observers have said has been used for espionage and to spread Russian propaganda. The head of Nato, Mark Rutte, said the organisation "stands in full solidarity with Germany". "The evidence is clear. And I welcome the measures announced by Germany in response," he wrote on X. The issue will be discussed at a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Ireland later on Tuesday. This breaking news story is being updated and more details will be published shortly. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/21/russ.text: President Vladimir Putin's United Russia party won a record number of 355 seats in Russia's 450-seat State Duma, the lower house of parliament, according to preliminary results released by electoral chief Ella Pamfilova on Monday.With almost all votes counted after the three-day election with no parties critical of Putin participating, results showed the presidential party will have a supermajority larger than its previous 2016 record of 343 seats.It was Russia's first parliamentary election since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.The Kremlin tightly controls elections and Moscow has banned criticism of its military campaign in Ukraine.Pamfilova said turnout was more than 59%, thanking Russians for voting despite what she called "psychological pressure" on the country.Russia's Communist party came second, winning 40 seats. The nationalist LDPR party took 25 seats and the New People party winning 20 seats.United Russia has dominated politics since the early 2000s and Putin has been in power since New Year's Eve 1999.Pamfilova said that more than 95% of votes have been counted and that final results will be announced later this week.Wave of Ukrainian dronesUkraine fired waves of drones at Moscow and the surrounding region on the final day of voting on Sunday, killing two people and setting an oil refinery on fire, officials said.Russia vowed it would "intensify" its strikes on Kyiv in response, with the defence ministry accusing Ukraine of attempting to "disrupt the democratic will of Russian citizens.""In response to the Kyiv regime's attacks on civilian targets within Russia, the Russian army will continue and intensify its high accuracy strikes against military targets in Kyiv," the Russian defence ministry said.The Ukrainian attack was the largest on Moscow since the start of the war and involved around 1,600 drones, 450 of which were aimed directly at the capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.Images showed a gaping hole in a multi-storey apartment building on the outskirts of the capital, while another showed black smoke billowing from what appeared to be an oil refinery.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised the attacks, saying "our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night."While diplomatic efforts to end the war have not prevented mutual strikes from escalating in recent months, Zelenskyy spoke by phone with US President Donald Trump, who in recent days has urged Kyiv to stop its attacks on Russian refineries.The pair are expected to meet in New York in the coming days.Ukraine has targeted Russian infrastructure with drones throughout the war, in retaliation for Russian bombardment of its own towns and cities.CyberattacksAs voting entered a final day, Russia's electoral chief said there had been a wave of cyberattacks targeting election infrastructure.Ella Pamfilova, chair of Russia's Central Election Commission, did not say who was responsible.The attacks appeared to have been carried out by "highly professional, well-coordinated groups using artificial intelligence tools," she said."Over the past period, more than 1,000 waves of DDoS attacks have been recorded against infrastructure in Russia that is specifically involved in the electoral process," Pamfilova was quoted as saying by Russian news agencies.DDoS (distributed denial-of-service) attacks involve overwhelming a system with internet traffic so that it is unable to function normally.She warned on Saturday that saboteurs had also severed communication lines in Russia's far east, in an apparent attempt to frustrate the voting.

https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: In case you missed the news last night, the Greens leader, Larissa Waters, has announced she will step down due to ill health. A party room meeting next week will be held to choose her successor, with the deputy leader, Mehreen Faruqi, and high-profile senators Sarah Hanson-Young, David Shoebridge and Nick McKim all possibilities to contest the leadership ballot. Waters said she had been managing a pre-existing kidney disease, but her health had “declined significantly over the course of recent months”. Her prognosis for recovery is positive, but she said the pressure of leadership was detracting from her focus on her health. She said: I’m really sad that illness means my time as leader has been cut short, but our movement needs a leader in good health to lead us to success at the next election. Passing the torch on to the next leader of the party will put them in the best position to take the Greens to the next election, fighting for people, not the corporate interests that run Labor,

Photograph: John Rivera/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images College football Air Force officer killed in rappelling accident before UTSA’s game against Navy Officer fell from rafters during pregame display Man treated on field before being taken to hospital Guardian sport Sun 18 Oct 2026 10.03 EDT Last modified on Sun 18 Oct 2026 10.09 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game against Navy on Saturday. The officer, who has not been named, was taking part in an event to celebrate UTSA’s Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans night. He fell on to the field while rappelling down from the stadium rafters. He was treated on the field before being taken away on a stretcher. He later died from his injuries at a local hospital. Nellis Air Force Base said he was part of the 6th Combat Training Squadron. The unit helps train military members to rappel down from helicopters. In video of the incident, the crowd could be heard reacting when the officer fell to the field. The Alamodome roof is around 170ft above the field. “There was something – you could just tell that the energy was just gone [from the crowd],” UTSA coach Jeff Traylor said after the game. “I’ve never had to deal with anything like that before. It just puts things in perspective. It really does.” The start of the game was delayed for around 10 minutes after the incident. “We are deeply saddened by the incident that occurred at the start of tonight’s game,” UTSA said in a statement. “Our heartfelt thoughts and prayers are with the soldier who was affected, his family and his military colleagues.” Explore more on these topics College football San Antonio College sports Texas US sports news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed Football Cricket Rugby union Tennis Cycling F1 Golf Boxing Rugby league Racing US sports
